decisions.reason: The hook revision may support campaign performance, but it does not change the lead-generation objective or target cost per lead.
Requiring a more direct, India-appropriate hook does not replace or alter the existing requirement for a viral creative style.
The source changes hook market alignment, not the candidate's 28–54 audience-age requirement; its Indian-market context is already represented.
Rejecting the drafted indirect approach does not necessarily revoke the independently created testimonial material or testimonial-style presentation.
The source changes the opening hook and messaging approach but does not modify the existing cut strategy.
Hook directness and Indian-market suitability do not alter lip-sync accuracy or facial-expression requirements.

The source rejects the submitted story-driven execution and requires a revised hook and reference-derived wording, but it does not necessarily revoke the client-confirmed original testimonial concept or no-copy constraint.
The statement that the approach will not work in India concerns messaging and hook suitability, not actor nationality or gender preference.
The candidate already records the same-message requirement to select and directly use relevant keywords from the reference videos; no additional state change is needed.
The hook revision does not resolve or change the production-method conflict concerning live-action versus AI-generated scenes.
The source addresses the opening hook and revised script wording, not the closing call to action.
The creative revision does not change the pilot video count, formats, duration, or conditional follow-on order.
